title: Symmetric structured-RNA motif panel for Prime Assembly
abstract: A synthetic primary research object that treats paired structured-RNA protection as a state-selective panel rather than a generic stability tag, with explicit measurements and a stopping rule.
disposition_reason: It most directly addresses the focused decision while preserving a discriminating test and a clear kill criterion.
nearest_prior_art: Component-level structured-RNA stabilization, without this synthetic paired-panel decision framing.
strongest_reason: The intervention and readout can separate assembly-state protection from bulk abundance.
weakest_causal_edge: The link between motif symmetry and productive complex residence remains unverified.
pairwise_summary: Not pairwise-ranked; the focused run compared decision roles directly.
reviewer_disagreement: Reviewers differed on feasibility, not on the value of the discriminating readout.
reviewer_critiques: Bulk abundance must not substitute for the assembly-proximal state.
Symmetry should be tested without changing unrelated expression features.
finalist_reason: Featured as the primary decision object without implying Arena selection or experimental validation.
reentry_condition: Not applicable while the object remains featured.
scientific_summary: A paired motif panel asks whether structured-RNA protection preserves a productive assembly state rather than merely increasing mature RNA abundance.
causal_mechanism: Matched motifs alter the residence-time distribution of intact RNA near the productive complex, changing product formation more strongly than bulk abundance.
evidence_basis: Synthetic component-level precedent only; the complete architecture is not claimed as experimentally demonstrated.
next_discriminating_experiment: Compare matched symmetric and control panels while measuring bulk abundance, assembly-proximal state, intended product, byproducts, and burden in the same series.
